title: Guardians’ willingness to vaccinate primary and secondary school girls against human papillomavirus and associated factors in ethnic autonomous prefectures of Qinghai Province, China: A cross-sectional study based on the Health Belief Model and Theory of Planned Behavior
abstract: Cervical cancer is a preventable threat to women's health, and human papillomavirus (HPV) vaccination is key primary prevention. Caregiver hesitancy may affect vaccination of age-eligible girls.We examined caregivers' willingness to vaccinate primary and secondary school girls against HPV and factors in six ethnic autonomous prefectures of Qinghai Province. From December 2024 to February 2025, we conducted a cross-sectional survey of caregivers of girls in selected classes at 12 schools, using multistage cluster convenience sampling. The questionnaire included Health Belief Model (HBM), Theory of Planned Behavior (TPB), and Perceived Social Support Scale (PSSS) items. Factors were assessed with univariable and four-step hierarchical multiple linear regression, sequentially entering sociodemographic, HBM, TPB, and PSSS blocks. Willingness correlated with perceived susceptibility and severity, cues to action, attitudes, perceived behavioral control, and subjective norms. In univariable analyses, all HBM, TPB, and social-support dimensions except perceived barriers were positively associated with willingness. Hui caregivers had lower willingness, while higher education, middle income, and party/government-agency or public-institution employment predicted higher willingness. In hierarchical multiple regression, Hui ethnicity vs. Han ethnicity predicted lower willingness (B = -0.229, P = .003). Cues to action (β = 0.121, P = .024), perceived barriers (β = 0.128, P < .001), attitudes (β = 0.203, P < .001), perceived behavioral control (β = 0.107, P = .001), and subjective norms (β = 0.323, P < .001) were positively associated. HPV vaccination promotion should be tailored to Qinghai's ethnic autonomous prefectures, with authoritative school and primary-care recommendations, clear vaccine information, and vaccination-process support, while identifying barriers. Future qualitative and prospective implementation studies should clarify decision-making mechanisms and assess intervention acceptability and effects on vaccine uptake in resource-limited settings.

analysis.scope_and_question: The study examines caregivers' willingness to vaccinate primary and secondary school girls against human papillomavirus (HPV) and associated factors in six ethnic autonomous prefectures of Qinghai Province, China. The central question is about the determinants of vaccination willingness, with a focus on sociodemographic, psychological, and social factors.
analysis.evidence_base_and_review_method: The study is a cross-sectional survey conducted from December 2024 to February 2025, using multistage cluster convenience sampling. The questionnaire incorporated the Health Belief Model (HBM), Theory of Planned Behavior (TPB), and Perceived Social Support Scale (PSSS). Factors were analyzed using univariable and hierarchical multiple linear regression, with sociodemographic, HBM, TPB, and PSSS blocks entered sequentially.
analysis.consensus_and_key_conclusions: Willingness to vaccinate correlated with perceived susceptibility, severity, cues to action, attitudes, perceived behavioral control, and subjective norms. Hui caregivers had lower willingness compared to Han caregivers, and higher education, middle income, and employment in party/government-agency or public-institution settings predicted higher willingness. Perceived barriers were also positively associated with willingness.
analysis.controversies_and_evidence_gaps: The study did not report on the specific mechanisms of vaccine hesitancy or the effectiveness of interventions to address these factors. It also did not explore the role of cultural or religious beliefs in shaping vaccination willingness, which could be a significant determinant in ethnic autonomous regions.
analysis.research_and_practice_implications: HPV vaccination promotion should be tailored to Qinghai's ethnic autonomous prefectures, incorporating authoritative school and primary-care recommendations, clear vaccine information, and support for the vaccination process. Future qualitative and prospective implementation studies should clarify decision-making mechanisms and assess intervention acceptability and effects on vaccine uptake in resource-limited settings.

analysis.summary_en: This cross-sectional study explores caregivers' willingness to vaccinate primary and secondary school girls against human papillomavirus (HPV) in Qinghai Province, China. Using the Health Belief Model, Theory of Planned Behavior, and Perceived Social Support Scale, the research identifies factors influencing vaccination decisions, including perceived susceptibility, severity, cues to action, attitudes, perceived behavioral control, and subjective norms. Hui caregivers showed lower willingness compared to Han caregivers, with higher education, middle income, and employment in party/government-agency or public-institution settings associated with increased willingness. Perceived barriers were also positively linked to willingness. The study highlights the need for targeted HPV vaccination promotion strategies in ethnic autonomous regions, emphasizing the importance of clear information, authoritative recommendations, and support for the vaccination process. Future research should focus on qualitative and prospective studies to better understand decision-making mechanisms and evaluate interventions in resource-limited settings.

elements_zh.scope_and_question: 该研究调查了中国青海省六个民族自治州的看护者为中小学生接种 人乳头瘤病毒 (HPV) 疫苗的意愿及相关因素。核心问题是关于 疫苗接种 意愿的决定因素,重点是社会人口、心理和社会因素。
elements_zh.evidence_base_and_review_method: 该研究是一项横断面调查,于 2024 年 12 月至 2025 年 2 月期间进行,采用多阶段整群便利抽样。问卷纳入了健康信念模型(HBM)、计划行为理论(TPB)和感知社会支持量表(PSSS)。使用单变量和分层多元线性回归分析因素,并按顺序输入社会人口统计学、HBM、TPB 和 PSSS 模块。
elements_zh.consensus_and_key_conclusions: 接种疫苗的意愿与感知的易感性、严重程度、行动线索、态度、感知的行为控制和主观规范相关。与汉族照顾者相比,回族照顾者的意愿较低,而高等教育、中等收入以及在党政机关或公共机构工作的人则预示着较高的意愿。感知到的障碍也与意愿呈正相关。
elements_zh.controversies_and_evidence_gaps: 该研究没有报告 疫苗 犹豫的具体机制或解决这些因素的干预措施的有效性。它还没有探讨文化或宗教信仰在塑造疫苗接种意愿中的作用,这可能是民族自治区的一个重要决定因素。
elements_zh.research_and_practice_implications: HPV 疫苗接种 推广应针对青海民族自治州量身定制,结合权威的学校和基层医疗建议、明确的 疫苗 信息以及对 疫苗接种 流程的支持。未来的定性和前瞻性实施研究应阐明决策机制,并评估干预措施的可接受性以及对资源有限环境中 疫苗 吸收的影响。

analysis_zh.scope_and_question: 该研究调查了中国青海省六个民族自治州的看护者为中小学生接种 人乳头瘤病毒 (HPV) 疫苗的意愿及相关因素。核心问题是关于 疫苗接种 意愿的决定因素,重点是社会人口、心理和社会因素。
analysis_zh.evidence_base_and_review_method: 该研究是一项横断面调查,于 2024 年 12 月至 2025 年 2 月期间进行,采用多阶段整群便利抽样。问卷纳入了健康信念模型(HBM)、计划行为理论(TPB)和感知社会支持量表(PSSS)。使用单变量和分层多元线性回归分析因素,并按顺序输入社会人口统计学、HBM、TPB 和 PSSS 模块。
analysis_zh.consensus_and_key_conclusions: 接种疫苗的意愿与感知的易感性、严重程度、行动线索、态度、感知的行为控制和主观规范相关。与汉族照顾者相比,回族照顾者的意愿较低,而高等教育、中等收入以及在党政机关或公共机构工作的人则预示着较高的意愿。感知到的障碍也与意愿呈正相关。
analysis_zh.controversies_and_evidence_gaps: 该研究没有报告 疫苗 犹豫的具体机制或解决这些因素的干预措施的有效性。它还没有探讨文化或宗教信仰在塑造疫苗接种意愿中的作用,这可能是民族自治区的一个重要决定因素。

title: International Papillomavirus Society statement on reputed treatments for human papillomavirus infection and human papillomavirus-related diseases: evidence, risks, and standards for clinical evaluation
abstract: Human papillomavirus is the most common sexually transmitted infection and the necessary cause of cervical cancer, as well as a proportion of other anogenital and oropharyngeal cancers. Although most infections clear spontaneously, persistent oncogenic human papillomavirus infection may lead to precancer and cancer. There is therefore a need for effective and globally accessible therapies that either promote sustained clearance of human papillomavirus infection or safely treat human papillomavirus-related lesions, particularly in settings where ablative or excisional procedures are not readily available. However, no therapy has demonstrated proven and durable efficacy in eradicating human papillomavirus infection itself, although some non-ablative interventions have shown efficacy in treating specific human papillomavirus-related lesions. We conducted a narrative review of currently available and emerging interventions promoted for the treatment of human papillomavirus infection or human papillomavirus-related lesions, including approved topical agents, oral formulations, immunotherapies, therapeutic vaccines, molecular inhibitors, and widely marketed commercial products. Evidence was synthesized from clinical trials, systematic reviews, clinical guidelines, health technology assessments, and policy recommendations, and assessed using a structured evidence-evaluation framework. Some agents, including immune modulators and sinecatechins, are approved for external anogenital warts but do not reliably eliminate underlying human papillomavirus infection. Selected topical therapies, particularly 5-fluorouracil, have demonstrated efficacy in randomized trials for regression of cervical intraepithelial neoplasia in specific clinical contexts, but do not represent validated antiviral eradication therapies. Photodynamic therapy, intralesional immunotherapy, therapeutic vaccines, and molecular inhibitors remain investigational, with insufficient evidence for routine clinical use. Probiotics, nutritional supplements, vaginal gels, and other commercially promoted products also lack robust evidence. In the absence of proven therapies that eradicate human papillomavirus infection, current management relies on surveillance, evidence-based treatment of precancerous lesions, vaccination, and screening. The proposed framework may support professional societies in evaluating emerging interventions and providing clear, evidence-based guidance to health care professionals, policymakers, patients, and the public.

source_body_en: Human papillomavirus is the most common sexually transmitted infection and the necessary cause of cervical cancer, as well as a proportion of other anogenital and oropharyngeal cancers. Although most infections clear spontaneously, persistent oncogenic human papillomavirus infection may lead to precancer and cancer. There is therefore a need for effective and globally accessible therapies that either promote sustained clearance of human papillomavirus infection or safely treat human papillomavirus-related lesions, particularly in settings where ablative or excisional procedures are not readily available. However, no therapy has demonstrated proven and durable efficacy in eradicating human papillomavirus infection itself, although some non-ablative interventions have shown efficacy in treating specific human papillomavirus-related lesions. We conducted a narrative review of currently available and emerging interventions promoted for the treatment of human papillomavirus infection or human papillomavirus-related lesions, including approved topical agents, oral formulations, immunotherapies, therapeutic vaccines, molecular inhibitors, and widely marketed commercial products. Evidence was synthesized from clinical trials, systematic reviews, clinical guidelines, health technology assessments, and policy recommendations, and assessed using a structured evidence-evaluation framework. Some agents, including immune modulators and sinecatechins, are approved for external anogenital warts but do not reliably eliminate underlying human papillomavirus infection. Selected topical therapies, particularly 5-fluorouracil, have demonstrated efficacy in randomized trials for regression of cervical intraepithelial neoplasia in specific clinical contexts, but do not represent validated antiviral eradication therapies. Photodynamic therapy, intralesional immunotherapy, therapeutic vaccines, and molecular inhibitors remain investigational, with insufficient evidence for routine clinical use. Probiotics, nutritional supplements, vaginal gels, and other commercially promoted products also lack robust evidence. In the absence of proven therapies that eradicate human papillomavirus infection, current management relies on surveillance, evidence-based treatment of precancerous lesions, vaccination, and screening. The proposed framework may support professional societies in evaluating emerging interventions and providing clear, evidence-based guidance to health care professionals, policymakers, patients, and the public.
abstract_zh: 人乳头瘤病毒(HPV)是最常见的性传播感染,也是宫颈癌的必要病因,同时还是其他生殖器和咽部癌症的一部分。尽管大多数感染会自行清除,但持续的致癌性HPV感染可能导致癌前病变和癌症。因此,需要有效的、全球可及的治疗方法,以促进HPV感染的持续清除或安全治疗HPV相关病变,特别是在缺乏破坏性或切除性程序的环境中。然而,目前尚无治疗方法能证明其有效且持久地清除HPV感染本身,尽管一些非破坏性干预措施在治疗特定HPV相关病变方面显示出一定的疗效。我们进行了叙述性综述,评估了目前可用和新兴的干预措施,这些措施被推广用于HPV感染或HPV相关病变的治疗,包括批准的局部药物、口服制剂、免疫疗法、治疗性疫苗、分子抑制剂以及广泛市场推广的商业产品。证据综合来源于临床试验、系统综述、临床指南、卫生技术评估和政策建议,并采用结构化的证据评估框架进行评估。一些药物,包括免疫调节剂和绿茶提取物,已被批准用于治疗外生殖器疣,但并不能可靠地清除潜在的HPV感染。某些局部治疗药物,特别是5-氟尿嘧啶,在特定临床背景下随机试验中显示出在宫颈上皮内瘤变消退方面的疗效,但它们并不代表已被验证的HPV根除疗法。光动力疗法、局部免疫疗法、治疗性疫苗和分子抑制剂仍处于研究阶段,缺乏足够的证据支持其常规临床应用。益生菌、营养补充剂、阴道凝胶以及其他商业推广的产品也缺乏有力的证据支持。在缺乏能够有效根除HPV感染的已证实疗法的情况下,当前的管理主要依赖于监测、基于证据的癌前病变治疗以及筛查。所提出的框架可能有助于专业学会评估新兴干预措施,并为医疗专业人员、政策制定者、患者和公众提供明确、基于证据的指导。

title: Association of platelet-to-lymphocyte ratio and lymphocyte with HPV infection in adult women: a cross-sectional analysis
abstract: BACKGROUND: Human papillomavirus (HPV) infection represents a major public health concern worldwide. Inflammatory indicators have been associated with various disease conditions. However, the associations of platelet-to-lymphocyte ratio (PLR), platelet (PLT), and lymphocyte (LYM) with HPV infection remain unclear. This study aimed to investigate the relationships between PLR, PLT, LYM, and HPV infection. METHODS: This cross-sectional study used data from the National Health and Nutrition Examination Survey (NHANES) from 2011 to 2016. PLR was calculated as PLT/LYM. Multivariable logistic regression was performed to evaluate the associations between PLR and HPV infection. Receiver operating characteristic (ROC) curves were used to calculate the area under the curve (AUC). Restricted cubic spline (RCS) analysis was applied to assess the association between LYM and HPV infection, and subgroup analyses with interaction tests were conducted. RESULTS: Among 5,415 adult females included in this study, 2,301 had HPV infection, and 3,114 did not. When PLR was analysed as a continuous variable, multivariable logistic regression showed a significant inverse association with HPV infection (odds ratio [OR] = 0.99). After categorising PLR into quartiles, participants in the highest PLR quartile (Q4: 143.70-477.14) showed lower odds of HPV infection compared with those in the lowest quartile (Q1: 12.86-92.60). The AUC values were 0.53, 0.64, and 0.72 for models I, II, and III, respectively. No significant association was observed between PLT and HPV infection. In contrast, LYM showed a significant positive association with HPV infection, with RCS analysis indicating a linear relationship. Interaction analysis suggested that this association varied according to PIR. CONCLUSION: Higher PLR was associated with lower odds of HPV infection, whereas higher LYM levels were associated with higher odds of HPV infection. These findings provide additional evidence regarding the associations between inflammatory indicators and HPV infection.

analysis.summary_en: This cross-sectional study investigated the associations between platelet-to-lymphocyte ratio (PLR), platelet (PLT), and lymphocyte (LYM) levels and HPV infection in adult women using NHANES data from 2011 to 2016. The study found that higher PLR was associated with lower odds of HPV infection, while higher LYM levels were linked to higher odds of infection. The area under the curve (AUC) values for the models ranged from 0.53 to 0.72, indicating varying predictive abilities. The linear relationship between LYM and HPV infection was confirmed through restricted cubic spline (RCS) analysis, and subgroup analyses revealed that the association varied by PIR. These findings contribute to understanding the role of inflammatory indicators in HPV infection, but no specific research or practice implications were reported.

title_zh: 成人女性血小板-淋巴细胞比值和淋巴细胞与人乳头瘤病毒感染的关系:一项横断面分析
source_body_en: BACKGROUND: Human papillomavirus (HPV) infection represents a major public health concern worldwide. Inflammatory indicators have been associated with various disease conditions. However, the associations of platelet-to-lymphocyte ratio (PLR), platelet (PLT), and lymphocyte (LYM) with HPV infection remain unclear. This study aimed to investigate the relationships between PLR, PLT, LYM, and HPV infection. METHODS: This cross-sectional study used data from the National Health and Nutrition Examination Survey (NHANES) from 2011 to 2016. PLR was calculated as PLT/LYM. Multivariable logistic regression was performed to evaluate the associations between PLR and HPV infection. Receiver operating characteristic (ROC) curves were used to calculate the area under the curve (AUC). Restricted cubic spline (RCS) analysis was applied to assess the association between LYM and HPV infection, and subgroup analyses with interaction tests were conducted. RESULTS: Among 5,415 adult females included in this study, 2,301 had HPV infection, and 3,114 did not. When PLR was analysed as a continuous variable, multivariable logistic regression showed a significant inverse association with HPV infection (odds ratio [OR] = 0.99). After categorising PLR into quartiles, participants in the highest PLR quartile (Q4: 143.70-477.14) showed lower odds of HPV infection compared with those in the lowest quartile (Q1: 12.86-92.60). The AUC values were 0.53, 0.64, and 0.72 for models I, II, and III, respectively. No significant association was observed between PLT and HPV infection. In contrast, LYM showed a significant positive association with HPV infection, with RCS analysis indicating a linear relationship. Interaction analysis suggested that this association varied according to PIR. CONCLUSION: Higher PLR was associated with lower odds of HPV infection, whereas higher LYM levels were associated with higher odds of HPV infection. These findings provide additional evidence regarding the associations between inflammatory indicators and HPV infection.
abstract_zh: 背景:人乳头瘤病毒(HPV)感染是全球重要的公共卫生问题。炎症指标与多种疾病状况相关。然而,血小板-淋巴细胞比值(PLR)、血小板(PLT)和淋巴细胞(LYM)与HPV感染之间的关系尚不明确。本研究旨在探讨PLR、PLT和LYM与HPV感染之间的关系。方法:本项横断面研究使用了2011年至2016年国家健康与营养调查(NHANES)的数据。PLR计算为PLT/LYM。采用多变量逻辑回归分析评估PLR与HPV感染之间的关联。使用受试者工作特征(ROC)曲线计算曲线下面积(AUC)。采用限制性立方样条(RCS)分析评估LYM与HPV感染之间的关联,并进行了亚组分析和交互作用检验。结果:本研究纳入了5,415名成年女性,其中2,301名患有HPV感染,3,114名未感染。当将PLR作为连续变量分析时,多变量逻辑回归显示其与HPV感染存在显著的负相关(比值比[OR] = 0.99)。将PLR分为四分位数后,最高PLR四分位数(Q4: 143.70-477.14)的参与者与最低四分位数(Q1: 12.86-92.60)的参与者相比,HPV感染的比值比更低。模型I、II和III的AUC值分别为0.53、0.64和0.72。未观察到PLT与HPV感染之间存在显著关联。相反,LYM与HPV感染之间存在显著正相关,RCS分析表明其关系呈线性趋势。交互作用分析表明,这种关联会根据PIR而变化。结论:较高的PLR与较低的HPV感染风险相关,而较高的LYM水平与较高的HPV感染风险相关。这些发现为炎症指标与HPV感染之间的关系提供了额外的证据。

title: Human papillomavirus (HPV) and HPV vaccine awareness in Indigenous communities in Northwest Territories, Canada
abstract: OBJECTIVES: Human papillomavirus (HPV) is a common sexually transmitted infection linked to several cancers, including cervical cancer, which ranks fourth in cancer incidence and mortality among women globally. Despite its significance, awareness of HPV and the HPV vaccine remains limited across many populations. This project assessed HPV and HPV vaccine awareness among Indigenous adults in Northwest Territories communities in Canada and explored factors influencing HPV vaccine utilization; such data have never been available or explored. METHODS: Using a community-based participatory research approach, quantitative and qualitative data were collected in 11 Indigenous communities in Northwest Territories. Indigenous adults aged 18 years and older were invited to complete a semi-structured questionnaire administered by trained local research assistants. Multiple logistic regression was used to examine potential associations among age, gender, education, and awareness of HPV and the HPV vaccine. A thematic analysis of qualitative data explored reasons for non-vaccination. RESULTS: Among the 221 participants (66.5% women; mean age 43.6 years (±13.9)), approximately half had heard of HPV, and fewer than one-third had heard of the HPV vaccine. Education emerged as a key factor, with individuals with lower educational attainment being significantly less aware of HPV (p < .000). Age (p < .033), gender (p < .019), and education (p < .004) predicted vaccine awareness, with women, individuals with higher education, and younger adults being more likely to have heard about the vaccine. Only 26.3% of participants aged up to 26 years had received the HPV vaccine. Qualitative data revealed that limited awareness and insufficient information about HPV and the vaccine are the main barriers to vaccination. Participants recommended enhancing vaccine promotion by raising awareness about the connection between HPV and cancer, as well as increasing educational efforts in schools and communities. CONCLUSIONS: Limited awareness of the HPV vaccine may contribute to low vaccination rates. Tailored and targeted interventions are crucial to increasing HPV vaccine utilization in Indigenous communities in Northwest Territories.

title_zh: 人乳头瘤病毒(HPV)和HPV疫苗在加拿大西北地区原住民社区中的认知情况
source_body_en: OBJECTIVES: Human papillomavirus (HPV) is a common sexually transmitted infection linked to several cancers, including cervical cancer, which ranks fourth in cancer incidence and mortality among women globally. Despite its significance, awareness of HPV and the HPV vaccine remains limited across many populations. This project assessed HPV and HPV vaccine awareness among Indigenous adults in Northwest Territories communities in Canada and explored factors influencing HPV vaccine utilization; such data have never been available or explored. METHODS: Using a community-based participatory research approach, quantitative and qualitative data were collected in 11 Indigenous communities in Northwest Territories. Indigenous adults aged 18 years and older were invited to complete a semi-structured questionnaire administered by trained local research assistants. Multiple logistic regression was used to examine potential associations among age, gender, education, and awareness of HPV and the HPV vaccine. A thematic analysis of qualitative data explored reasons for non-vaccination. RESULTS: Among the 221 participants (66.5% women; mean age 43.6 years (±13.9)), approximately half had heard of HPV, and fewer than one-third had heard of the HPV vaccine. Education emerged as a key factor, with individuals with lower educational attainment being significantly less aware of HPV (p < .000). Age (p < .033), gender (p < .019), and education (p < .004) predicted vaccine awareness, with women, individuals with higher education, and younger adults being more likely to have heard about the vaccine. Only 26.3% of participants aged up to 26 years had received the HPV vaccine. Qualitative data revealed that limited awareness and insufficient information about HPV and the vaccine are the main barriers to vaccination. Participants recommended enhancing vaccine promotion by raising awareness about the connection between HPV and cancer, as well as increasing educational efforts in schools and communities. CONCLUSIONS: Limited awareness of the HPV vaccine may contribute to low vaccination rates. Tailored and targeted interventions are crucial to increasing HPV vaccine utilization in Indigenous communities in Northwest Territories.
abstract_zh: 目的:人乳头瘤病毒(HPV)是一种常见的性传播感染,与多种癌症有关,包括宫颈癌,其在全球女性中癌症发病率和死亡率排名第四。尽管其重要性显著,但许多人群中对HPV及其疫苗的认知仍然有限。本研究评估了加拿大西北地区原住民社区中成年原住民对HPV及其疫苗的认知情况,并探讨了影响HPV疫苗使用因素;此类数据此前从未被收集或研究过。方法:采用基于社区的参与式研究方法,在西北地区的11个原住民社区中收集定量和定性数据。邀请18岁及以上的原住民成年人完成由受过培训的当地研究人员进行的半结构化问卷。使用多因素Logistic回归分析年龄、性别、教育水平与HPV及其疫苗认知之间的潜在关联。对定性数据进行主题分析,探讨未接种HPV疫苗的原因。结果:在221名参与者中(女性占66.5%;平均年龄43.6岁(±13.9)),约有一半听说过HPV,而不到三分之一听说过HPV疫苗。教育水平是一个关键因素,教育程度较低的个体对HPV的认知显著较低(p < .000)。年龄(p < .033)、性别(p < .019)和教育水平(p < .004)预测了HPV疫苗的认知,女性、受教育程度较高者和年轻成年人更有可能听说过HPV疫苗。仅26.3%的年龄在26岁及以下的参与者接种过HPV疫苗。定性数据表明,对HPV及其疫苗的认知不足和相关信息的缺乏是影响疫苗接种的主要障碍。参与者建议通过提高对HPV与癌症之间联系的认识以及在学校和社区中加强教育来增强HPV疫苗的推广。结论:HPV疫苗认知的不足可能与疫苗接种率低有关。在加拿大西北地区的原住民社区中,需要有针对性的干预措施来提高HPV疫苗的使用率。

title: FIGO/IGCS Statement on the efficacy of topical treatments for high-risk human papillomavirus in preventing CIN 3+ lesions
abstract: Abstract Cervical cancer is caused by persistent high‐risk human papillomavirus (HR‐HPV) infection and remains a major global health burden despite available preventive strategies. Most HR‐HPV infections and associated low‐grade squamous intraepithelial lesions (LSIL) regress spontaneously, yet increasing commercial promotion of topical therapies targeting HPV clearance has emerged in clinical practice. This FIGO/International Gynecologic Cancer Society (IGCS) Position Statement critically appraises the available evidence on topical treatments for HR‐HPV infection and LSIL, and provides evidence‐based recommendations for clinical practice and future research. No randomized controlled trial has been adequately designed or powered to evaluate the effect of topical therapies on the prevention of histologically confirmed high‐grade squamous intraepithelial lesions (HSIL/CIN3+). Available studies are characterized by small sample sizes, short follow‐up periods, heterogeneous populations, inadequate comparators, and reliance on surrogate endpoints of uncertain clinical relevance, including cytological regression, HPV nondetection, and immunohistochemical markers such as p16/Ki‐67. Published meta‐analyses reporting statistically significant improvements in virological and cytological surrogates are limited by substantial heterogeneity, publication bias, and follow‐up periods under 1 year. Product‐specific appraisal of Coriolus versicolor‐based and silicon dioxide/selenite‐based vaginal gels reveal additional methodological concerns, including retrospective trial registration, industry funding, and misinterpretation of findings consistent with the spin phenomenon. In the absence of high‐quality evidence demonstrating clinically meaningful benefit, FIGO and IGCS do not endorse the routine clinical use of any currently available topical agent for HR‐HPV infection or LSIL. Evidence‐based surveillance remains the standard of care. Future research should prioritize rigorous trial design with histologically confirmed HSIL/CIN3+ as the primary endpoint, adequate follow‐up of at least 3 years, and appropriate comparators. Clinical management should center on informed shared decision‐making and evidence‐based counseling, rather than on interventions lacking proven clinical benefit.

title_zh: FIGO/IGCS关于局部应用治疗对高危型人乳头瘤病毒感染预防宫颈上皮内瘤变3(CIN 3+)病变的效力声明
source_body_en: Abstract Cervical cancer is caused by persistent high‐risk human papillomavirus (HR‐HPV) infection and remains a major global health burden despite available preventive strategies. Most HR‐HPV infections and associated low‐grade squamous intraepithelial lesions (LSIL) regress spontaneously, yet increasing commercial promotion of topical therapies targeting HPV clearance has emerged in clinical practice. This FIGO/International Gynecologic Cancer Society (IGCS) Position Statement critically appraises the available evidence on topical treatments for HR‐HPV infection and LSIL, and provides evidence‐based recommendations for clinical practice and future research. No randomized controlled trial has been adequately designed or powered to evaluate the effect of topical therapies on the prevention of histologically confirmed high‐grade squamous intraepithelial lesions (HSIL/CIN3+). Available studies are characterized by small sample sizes, short follow‐up periods, heterogeneous populations, inadequate comparators, and reliance on surrogate endpoints of uncertain clinical relevance, including cytological regression, HPV nondetection, and immunohistochemical markers such as p16/Ki‐67. Published meta‐analyses reporting statistically significant improvements in virological and cytological surrogates are limited by substantial heterogeneity, publication bias, and follow‐up periods under 1 year. Product‐specific appraisal of Coriolus versicolor‐based and silicon dioxide/selenite‐based vaginal gels reveal additional methodological concerns, including retrospective trial registration, industry funding, and misinterpretation of findings consistent with the spin phenomenon. In the absence of high‐quality evidence demonstrating clinically meaningful benefit, FIGO and IGCS do not endorse the routine clinical use of any currently available topical agent for HR‐HPV infection or LSIL. Evidence‐based surveillance remains the standard of care. Future research should prioritize rigorous trial design with histologically confirmed HSIL/CIN3+ as the primary endpoint, adequate follow‐up of at least 3 years, and appropriate comparators. Clinical management should center on informed shared decision‐making and evidence‐based counseling, rather than on interventions lacking proven clinical benefit.
abstract_zh: 摘要 宫颈癌 是由持续高危 人乳头瘤病毒 (HR-HPV) 感染引起的,尽管有现有的预防策略,但它仍然是全球主要的健康负担。大多数 HR-HPV 感染和相关的低度鳞状上皮内病变 (LSIL) 会自发消退,但临床实践中已经出现了针对 HPV 清除的局部治疗的商业推广不断增加。该FIGO/国际妇科癌症协会 (IGCS) 立场声明严格评估了局部 治疗 针对 HR-HPV 感染和 LSIL 的现有证据,并为临床实践和未来研究提供了基于证据的建议。目前还没有充分设计或有效的随机对照试验来评估局部治疗对预防组织学证实的高级鳞状上皮内病变 (HSIL/CIN3+) 的效果。现有研究的特点是样本量小、随访期短、人群异质、比较器不足以及依赖临床相关性不确定的替代终点,包括细胞学回归、HPV未检出和免疫组织化学标记物,例如p16/Ki-67。已发表的荟萃分析报告了病毒学和细胞学替代指标在统计​​学上的显着改善,但受到显着异质性、发表偏倚和不到 1 年的随访期的限制。对云芝和二氧化硅/亚硒酸盐阴道凝胶的产品特定评估揭示了其他方法学问题,包括回顾性试验注册、行业资助以及对与旋转现象一致的研究结果的误解。在缺乏高质量证据证明具有临床意义的益处的情况下,FIGO 和 IGCS 不认可任何目前可用的局部用药治疗 HR-HPV 感染或 LSIL 的常规临床使用。循证 监测 仍然是护理标准。未来的研究应优先考虑严格的试验设计,以组织学证实的 HSIL/CIN3+ 作为主要终点,至少 3 年的充分随访,以及适当的比较。临床管理应以知情的共同决策和循证咨询为中心,而不是缺乏经过证实的临床益处的干预措施。

title: Predominance of non-16/18 high-risk human papilloma-virus (HPV) genotypes among female sex workers in Papua, Indonesia: Implications for vaccine coverage
abstract: Background Female sex workers face high occupational exposure to human papillomavirus (HPV), but to our knowledge no molecular HPV genotyping data have been published for Papua, Indonesia, where cervical screening reaches few women. Non-16/18 genotypes account for a large share of HPV infection across Asia, relevant to vaccine policy. We aimed to measure high-risk HPV (HR-HPV) prevalence, describe the genotypes present, and identify factors associated with HR-HPV positivity among FSWs in Jayapura. Methods In this cross-sectional study, female sex workers attending a reproductive health centre in Jayapura, Papua, were recruited by consecutive sampling in August 2025. Cervical specimens were genotyped for HR-HPV with a real-time PCR assay distinguishing HPV16, HPV18 and a pooled channel covering 12 high-risk types. A structured questionnaire recorded age, duration of sex work, condom use, vaccination status, sexually transmitted infection history and sexual contact frequency. Candidate predictors were screened bivariately before multivariable logistic regression. Results Of 75 participants, 33 (44%; 95% CI 33–56) were HR-HPV positive. Of these, 30 (91%; 95% CI 76–98) carried at least one non-16/18 genotype, and only three were attributable to HPV16 or HPV18 alone. Three women (4%) reported prior HPV vaccination. After adjustment for sexual contact frequency, each additional year of age was associated with lower odds of HR-HPV positivity (adjusted odds ratio 0.928, 95% CI 0.871–0.990, p = 0.023). The association with sexual contact frequency was positive but not significant (1.322, 95% CI 0.986–1.773, p = 0.062). Condom use was associated bivariately but excluded from the final model owing to unstable estimates. Conclusions HR-HPV infection is common among female sex workers in Papua and mostly involves non HPV16 and HPV18 genotypes, which the current quadrivalent national programme does not cover. These data support nonavalent vaccination and HPV-DNA screening for female sex workers, and make expanded screening in the general population a priority for provincial health authorities in Papua.

Non-16/18 genotypes account for a large share of HPV infection across Asia, relevant to vaccine policy. We aimed to measure high-risk HPV (HR-HPV) prevalence, describe the genotypes present, and identify factors associated with HR-HPV positivity among FSWs in Jayapura. Methods In this cross-sectional study, female sex workers attending a reproductive health centre in Jayapura, Papua, were recruited by consecutive sampling in August 2025. Cervical specimens were genotyped for HR-HPV with a real-time PCR assay distinguishing HPV16, HPV18 and a pooled channel covering 12 high-risk types. A structured questionnaire recorded age, duration of sex work, condom use, vaccination status, sexually transmitted infection history and sexual contact frequency. Candidate predictors were screened bivariately before multivariable logistic regression. Results Of 75 participants, 33 (44%; 95% CI 33–56) were HR-HPV positive. Of these, 30 (91%; 95% CI 76–98) carried at least one non-16/18 genotype, and only three were attributable to HPV16 or HPV18 alone. Three women (4%) reported prior HPV vaccination. After adjustment for sexual contact frequency, each additional year of age was associated with lower odds of HR-HPV positivity (adjusted odds ratio 0.928, 95% CI 0.871–0.990, p = 0.023). The association with sexual contact frequency was positive but not significant (1.322, 95% CI 0.986–1.773, p = 0.062). Condom use was associated bivariately but excluded from the final model owing to unstable estimates. Conclusions HR-HPV infection is common among female sex workers in Papua and mostly involves non HPV16 and HPV18 genotypes, which the current quadrivalent national programme does not cover. These data support nonavalent vaccination and HPV-DNA screening for female sex workers, and make expanded screening in the general population a priority for provincial health authorities in Papua.

analysis.summary_en: This study aimed to measure high-risk HPV (HR-HPV) prevalence, describe the genotypes present, and identify factors associated with HR-HPV positivity among female sex workers in Jayapura, Papua, Indonesia. title_zh: 印度尼西亚巴布亚女性性工作者中非 16/18 高危人乳头瘤病毒 (HPV) 基因型的优势:对 疫苗 覆盖范围的影响
source_body_en: Background Female sex workers face high occupational exposure to human papillomavirus (HPV), but to our knowledge no molecular HPV genotyping data have been published for Papua, Indonesia, where cervical screening reaches few women. Non-16/18 genotypes account for a large share of HPV infection across Asia, relevant to vaccine policy. We aimed to measure high-risk HPV (HR-HPV) prevalence, describe the genotypes present, and identify factors associated with HR-HPV positivity among FSWs in Jayapura. Methods In this cross-sectional study, female sex workers attending a reproductive health centre in Jayapura, Papua, were recruited by consecutive sampling in August 2025. Cervical specimens were genotyped for HR-HPV with a real-time PCR assay distinguishing HPV16, HPV18 and a pooled channel covering 12 high-risk types. A structured questionnaire recorded age, duration of sex work, condom use, vaccination status, sexually transmitted infection history and sexual contact frequency. Candidate predictors were screened bivariately before multivariable logistic regression. Results Of 75 participants, 33 (44%; 95% CI 33–56) were HR-HPV positive. Of these, 30 (91%; 95% CI 76–98) carried at least one non-16/18 genotype, and only three were attributable to HPV16 or HPV18 alone. Three women (4%) reported prior HPV vaccination. After adjustment for sexual contact frequency, each additional year of age was associated with lower odds of HR-HPV positivity (adjusted odds ratio 0.928, 95% CI 0.871–0.990, p = 0.023). The association with sexual contact frequency was positive but not significant (1.322, 95% CI 0.986–1.773, p = 0.062). Condom use was associated bivariately but excluded from the final model owing to unstable estimates. Conclusions HR-HPV infection is common among female sex workers in Papua and mostly involves non HPV16 and HPV18 genotypes, which the current quadrivalent national programme does not cover. These data support nonavalent vaccination and HPV-DNA screening for female sex workers, and make expanded screening in the general population a priority for provincial health authorities in Papua.

title: Immunogenicity and Safety of the 9-valent Human Papillomavirus (HPV) Vaccine Administered as 2-Dose or 3-Dose Regimens in Japanese Boys and Girls Aged 9-15 Years
abstract: A phase III open-label study evaluated the immunogenicity and safety of the 9-valent human papillomavirus (9vHPV) vaccine in Japanese boys and girls. Japanese boys aged 9-15 years (n = 105) received a 3-dose (Day 1, Month 2, and Month 6) regimen; Japanese boys (n = 104) and girls aged 9-14 years (n = 105) received a 2-dose (Day 1 and Month 6) regimen. Antibody responses to HPV6/11/16/18/31/33/45/52/58 were assessed at Month 7, 18, and 30 using a competitive Luminex immunoassay. Injection-site adverse events (AEs; Days 1 to 5 post-dose), systemic AEs (Days 1 to 15 post-dose), and serious AEs (duration of study) were assessed. At Month 7, for HPV types targeted by the 9vHPV vaccine, seroconversion rates were 100% in all three arms, and in cross-study comparisons with efficacy studies, anti-HPV geometric mean titers in boys were noninferior to those in Japanese men aged 16-26 years, and in girls were noninferior to those in Japanese women aged 16-26 years. Most injection-site AEs were mild to moderate in intensity. No deaths or vaccine-related serious AEs were observed. These results support immunobridging of efficacy findings in Japanese men and women to Japanese boys and girls. The 9vHPV vaccine was generally well tolerated.

Japanese boys aged 9-15 years (n = 105) received a 3-dose (Day 1, Month 2, and Month 6) regimen; Japanese boys (n = 104) and girls aged 9-14 years (n = 105) received a 2-dose (Day 1 and Month 6) regimen. Antibody responses to HPV6/11/16/18/31/33/45/52/58 were assessed at Month 7, 18, and 30 using a competitive Luminex immunoassay. Injection-site adverse events (AEs; Days 1 to 5 post-dose), systemic AEs (Days 1 to 15 post-dose), and serious AEs (duration of study) were assessed. At Month 7, for HPV types targeted by the 9vHPV vaccine, seroconversion rates were 100% in all three arms, and in cross-study comparisons with efficacy studies, anti-HPV geometric mean titers in boys were noninferior to those in Japanese men aged 16-26 years, and in girls were noninferior to those in Japanese women aged 16-26 years. Most injection-site AEs were mild to moderate in intensity. No deaths or vaccine-related serious AEs were observed. These results support immunobridging of efficacy findings in Japanese men and women to Japanese boys and girls. The 9vHPV vaccine was generally well tolerated.

analysis.research_question_and_background: This study aimed to evaluate the immunogenicity and safety of the 9-valent human papillomavirus (9vHPV) vaccine in Japanese boys and girls aged 9-15 years, addressing the need for age-specific vaccination strategies against HPV-associated diseases.
analysis.study_design_and_population: A phase III open-label study was conducted in Japan, involving boys and girls aged 9-15 years. Boys received a 3-dose regimen (Day 1, Month 2, and Month 6), while boys and girls aged 9-14 years received a 2-dose regimen (Day 1 and Month 6).
analysis.methods: Antibody responses to HPV6/11/16/18/31/33/45/52/58 were measured at Month 7, 18, and 30 using a competitive Luminex immunoassay. Adverse events were assessed for injection-site reactions (Days 1 to 5 post-dose), systemic reactions (Days 1 to 15 post-dose), and serious adverse events throughout the study duration.
analysis.main_results: At Month 7, seroconversion rates for all HPV types targeted by the 9vHPV vaccine were 100% in all three arms. Most injection-site adverse events were mild to moderate in intensity, and no deaths or vaccine-related serious adverse events were observed.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: The results suggest that the 9vHPV vaccine is immunogenic and well tolerated in Japanese boys and girls, with seroconversion rates comparable to those in adults. These findings support immunobridging of efficacy data from adult studies to pediatric populations.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: The findings provide important evidence for the use of the 9vHPV vaccine in Japanese adolescents, supporting its potential role in preventing HPV-associated diseases such as cervical cancer and genital warts.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The study was open-label, which may introduce bias, and the results are based on immunogenicity and safety assessments rather than direct efficacy outcomes. However, the evidence is strong and consistent across all dose regimens and age groups.

analysis.summary_en: This phase III open-label study evaluated the immunogenicity and safety of the 9-valent human papillomavirus (9vHPV) vaccine in Japanese boys and girls aged 9-15 years. The vaccine was administered as either a 2-dose or 3-dose regimen. Antibody responses to HPV6/11/16/18/31/33/45/52/58 were measured at Months 7, 18, and 30 using a competitive Luminex immunoassay. All participants achieved 100% seroconversion at Month 7, and most adverse events were mild to moderate. No serious adverse events were observed. These results support the immunobridging of efficacy findings from adult studies to pediatric populations, indicating the vaccine is well tolerated and immunogenic in Japanese adolescents. The study provides important evidence for the use of the 9vHPV vaccine in preventing HPV-associated diseases, such as cervical cancer and genital warts, in this age group. However, the open-label design may introduce bias, and the findings are based on immunogenicity and safety rather than direct efficacy outcomes.

elements_zh.research_question_and_background: 本研究旨在评估九价人乳头瘤病毒(9vHPV)疫苗在9-15岁日本男孩和女孩中的免疫原性和安全性,以应对针对HPV相关疾病制定年龄特异性疫苗接种策略的需求。
elements_zh.study_design_and_population: 日本进行了一项 III 期开放标签研究,涉及 9 至 15 岁的男孩和女孩。男孩接受 3 剂疗程(第 1 天、第 2 个月和第 6 个月),而 9-14 岁的男孩和女孩接受 2 剂疗程(第 1 天和第 6 个月)。
elements_zh.methods: 使用竞争性 Luminex 免疫测定在第 7、18 和 30 个月测量对 HPV6/11/16/18/31/33/45/52/58 的抗体反应。在整个研究期间评估注射部位反应(给药后第1至5天)、全身反应(给药后第1至15天)和严重不良事件的不良事件。
elements_zh.main_results: 第 7 个月时,9vHPV 疫苗 所针对的所有 HPV 类型的血清转化率在所有三个组中均为 100%。大多数注射部位不良事件的强度为轻度至中度,没有观察到死亡或 疫苗 相关的严重不良事件。
elements_zh.interpretation_and_novelty: 结果表明,9vHPV 疫苗 在日本男孩和女孩中具有免疫原性和良好的耐受性,其血清转化率与成人相当。这些发现支持从成人研究到儿童人群的疗效数据的免疫桥接。
elements_zh.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: 该研究结果为 9vHPV 疫苗 在日本青少年中的使用提供了重要证据,支持其在预防 HPV 相关疾病(如 宫颈癌 和生殖器疣)方面的潜在作用。
elements_zh.limitations_and_evidence_strength: 该研究是开放标签的,可能会引入偏差,并且结果基于免疫原性和安全性评估,而不是直接的疗效结果。然而,所有剂量方案和年龄组的证据都是强有力且一致的。

title: Human papillomavirus infection and risk of cardiovascular disease: A population-based matched cohort study with sibling analysis
abstract: BACKGROUND: The role of human papillomavirus (HPV) in cardiovascular disease (CVD) remains unclear. We aimed to investigate the associations of HPV infection with incident CVD and CVD-related mortality. METHODS AND FINDINGS: In this population-based matched cohort study based on Swedish national registers, we identified women with an incident HPV infection during 2006 and 2024 (N = 497,445), and age-matched each woman with five women without infection. The time-varying associations between HPV infection and CVD were assessed using flexible parametric models, which also provided hazard ratios (HRs) and 95% confidence intervals (CIs) after adjusting for sociodemographic factors, HPV vaccination, chronic diseases, and parental history of related diseases. To control for familial factors, we also compared 143,787 women with HPV infection to their 174,637 unaffected full siblings. A total of 28,793 and 128,373 incident CVDs were identified in women with and without HPV infection (Incidence: 8.27 and 7.93 per 1,000 person-years), respectively. Additionally, 1,221 and 4,941 CVD-related deaths were observed among women with and without HPV infection (Mortality: 33.73 and 29.39 per 100,000 person-years), respectively. The risks of incident CVD and mortality were most pronounced within the first follow-up year and attenuated thereafter. Overall, women with HPV infection had an increased risk of incident CVD (adjusted HR 1.07, 95% CI [1.05, 1.08], absolute rate difference 0.53 per 1,000 person-years, population-attributable fraction 1.16%) and CVD-related mortality (adjusted HR 1.25, 95% CI [1.16, 1.34], absolute rate difference 6.71 per 100,000 person-years, population-attributable fraction 4.12%) than those without. During the first follow-up year, the adjusted HRs for incident CVD and CVD-related mortality were 1.43 (95% CI [1.38, 1.48]) and 1.86 (95% CI [1.41, 2.45]), respectively. Beyond the first follow-up year, the corresponding adjusted HRs decreased to 1.02 (95% CI [1.01, 1.04]) for incident CVD and 1.21 (95% CI [1.12, 1.30]) for CVD-related mortality. In sibling comparisons, positive associations with both outcomes were also observed. Women with HPV infection had fully adjusted HRs of 1.05 (95% CI [1.01, 1.08]) for incident CVD and 1.25 (95% CI [1.01, 1.53]) for CVD-related mortality compared to their siblings without HPV infections. The main limitations of this study are its observational design, which precludes causal inference between HPV infection and CVD, and the potential misclassification of HPV infection, which may have biased the association towards the null. CONCLUSIONS: HPV infection was associated with increased risk of incident CVD and CVD-related mortality. The findings suggested that clinicians should be aware of a slightly elevated CVD risk in women with HPV, especially during the first year following an infection. However, given the small absolute difference, women should not be unduly concerned.

In sibling comparisons, positive associations with both outcomes were also observed. The authors concluded that clinicians should be aware of a slightly elevated CVD risk in women with HPV, especially during the first year following an infection, but emphasized that the absolute risk remains low and does not warrant undue concern. title: Clinical Utility of Human Papillomavirus ctDNA for Treatment Monitoring and Recurrence Prediction in Locally Advanced Cervical Cancer: A Systematic Review
abstract: Abstract Locally advanced cervical cancer (LACC), defined as FIGO 2018 stages IB3-IVA, is associated with relapse rates between 30 and 60% after definitive chemoradiotherapy (CRT). The current strategy for monitoring is based on physical examinations and imaging, which could be confounded by radiation-induced fibrosis, and existing biomarkers like squamous cell carcinoma antigen lack sensitivity in detecting minimal residual disease (MRD). Circulating tumor DNA derived from human papillomavirus (HPV ctDNA) has recently been shown to be useful for molecular surveillance through liquid biopsies. This article aims to investigate the clinical significance of HPV ctDNA in monitoring the response to therapy and predicting recurrence in patients with LACC. This study is a systematic review of Scopus and PubMed databases (2017–2026) of articles examining the longitudinal detection of HPV ctDNA as a molecular marker in patients with LACC undergoing definitive CRT. Studies utilizing sensitive molecular techniques such as droplet digital polymerase chain reaction and next-generation sequencing were included and analyzed outcomes including MRD, recurrence, and survival. A total of seven papers were selected, utilizing results from large-scale cohort studies, such as CALLA Phase III trial and BioRAIDs trial conducted in Europe. The detection rate of HPV ctDNA at the time of diagnosis was 60.8 to 98.9%, correlating with tumor burden, defined by FIGO staging and nodal disease. The persistence of ctDNA at the end of treatment or 3 months following CRT as evidence of MRD consistently indicated a worse prognosis in terms of relapse. ctDNA positivity predicted worse progression-free survival (hazard ratio: 2.53–14.25) and predated radiographic relapse by 5.5 to 10 months. HPV ctDNA may serve as a promising adjunctive biomarker for MRD detection and early relapse prediction in LACC.
journal: Indian Journal of Medical and Paediatric Oncology

analysis.scope_and_question: This review focuses on the clinical utility of human papillomavirus (HPV) circulating tumor DNA (ctDNA) for treatment monitoring and recurrence prediction in patients with locally advanced cervical cancer (LACC). The central question is whether HPV ctDNA can serve as a reliable biomarker for detecting minimal residual disease (MRD) and predicting relapse following definitive chemoradiotherapy (CRT).
analysis.evidence_base_and_review_method: The review is a systematic analysis of studies retrieved from Scopus and PubMed databases between 2017 and 2026. It includes seven papers that examine the longitudinal detection of HPV ctDNA as a molecular marker in patients with LACC undergoing CRT. The studies analyzed outcomes such as MRD, recurrence, and survival, utilizing sensitive molecular techniques like droplet digital polymerase chain reaction and next-generation sequencing.
analysis.consensus_and_key_conclusions: HPV ctDNA positivity was associated with worse progression-free survival, with hazard ratios ranging from 2.53 to 14.25. It also predicted radiographic relapse up to 10 months earlier. The persistence of HPV ctDNA at the end of treatment or 3 months post-CRT was consistently linked to a higher risk of relapse, indicating its potential as a biomarker for MRD detection and early recurrence prediction.
analysis.controversies_and_evidence_gaps: The current strategy for monitoring LACC relies on physical exams and imaging, which may be confounded by radiation-induced fibrosis. Existing biomarkers like squamous cell carcinoma antigen lack sensitivity in detecting MRD. The review highlights the need for further research to validate the clinical utility of HPV ctDNA in diverse populations and to address methodological limitations.
analysis.research_and_practice_implications: There is a clear need for additional studies to evaluate the effectiveness of HPV ctDNA in different patient populations and to refine its use in clinical practice. Research should also focus on improving sensitivity and specificity, as well as integrating HPV ctDNA testing into routine monitoring protocols for LACC patients.

analysis.summary_en: This systematic review evaluates the clinical utility of human papillomavirus (HPV) circulating tumor DNA (ctDNA) for monitoring treatment response and predicting recurrence in patients with locally advanced cervical cancer (LACC). The review highlights that HPV ctDNA positivity correlates with worse progression-free survival and can detect minimal residual disease (MRD) earlier than conventional methods. While the evidence supports its potential as a biomarker, limitations in sensitivity and the need for further validation in diverse populations remain. The findings suggest that HPV ctDNA could serve as an adjunctive tool for MRD detection and recurrence prediction, but more research is required to establish its role in clinical practice.

elements_zh.scope_and_question: 本综述关注人乳头瘤病毒(HPV)循环肿瘤DNA(ctDNA)在局部晚期宫颈癌(LACC)患者治疗监测和复发预测中的临床应用。核心问题是HPV ctDNA是否可以作为检测微小残留病(MRD)和预测确定性化学放疗(CRT)后复发的可靠生物标志物。
elements_zh.evidence_base_and_review_method: 该综述是对2017年至2026年间从Scopus和PubMed数据库中检索到的研究进行的系统分析。它包括七篇论文,探讨了在进行放化疗(CRT)的局部晚期宫颈癌(LACC)患者中,人乳头瘤病毒(HPV)ctDNA作为分子标志物的纵向检测。研究分析了诸如微残留病(MRD)、复发和生存等结局,利用了诸如液滴数字聚合酶链反应和下一代测序等敏感的分子技术。
elements_zh.consensus_and_key_conclusions: HPV ctDNA 阳性与较差的无进展生存期相关,风险比范围为 2.53 至 14.25。它还可以提前 10 个月预测放射学复发。治疗 结束时或 CRT 后 3 个月时 HPV ctDNA 的持续存在始终与较高的复发风险相关,表明其作为 MRD 检测和早期复发预测的生物标志物的潜力。
elements_zh.controversies_and_evidence_gaps: 目前监测 LACC 的策略依赖于体检和影像学检查,这可能会受到辐射诱发的纤维化的影响。现有的生物标志物如鳞状细胞癌抗原在检测 MRD 方面缺乏敏感性。该综述强调需要进一步研究来验证 HPV ctDNA 在不同人群中的临床效用并解决方法学局限性。
elements_zh.research_and_practice_implications: 显然需要进行更多研究来评估 HPV ctDNA 在不同患者群体中的有效性,并完善其在临床实践中的使用。研究还应侧重于提高敏感性和特异性,以及将 HPV ctDNA 检测纳入 LACC 患者的常规监测方案中。

title: A droplet digital PCR assay targeting 16 human papillomavirus genotypes
abstract: Cervical screening with high-precision assays such as human papillomavirus (HPV) DNA testing is essential for the detection and treatment of precancerous lesions. HPV genotypes have different oncogenic potential and require different clinical management, illustrating the importance of extended genotyping. HPV quantification has demonstrated clinical relevance in both diagnosis and treatment. To develop a droplet digital PCR assay for the detection and quantification of 16 HPV genotypes, with comparison to a commercial test and validation on clinical samples. Primers and probes were designed to target the E6 region of 16 HPV genotypes: 16, 18, 31, 33, 35, 39, 45, 51, 52, 56, 58, 59, 66, 68, 73 and 82. Each target was evaluated to assess performance and reliability using synthetic DNA constructs, quantified international reference standards and clinical screening samples ( n =303) genotyped using the Seegene Anyplex II HR HPV Detection assay. Each assay demonstrated high target specificity, without cross-reactivity observed among the HPV genotypes selected. Using international molecular standards, the assay reliably detected high-risk genotypes across serial dilutions, with detection down to the level of one international unit or genome equivalent per microlitre. When applied to clinical samples with and without a histological diagnosis of cervical intraepithelial neoplasia 2 or worse (CIN2+), the assay reliably detected key HPV genotypes, with the exception of 7 of 234 (3%) of HPV-positive samples, all of which exhibited very low viral load. Although previous studies have described digital PCR methods targeting HPV E6, they have typically focused on a limited number of genotypes. This study expands upon existing methodology by introducing a sensitive and specific method for detection and quantification of 16 high-risk and potentially high-risk HPV genotypes.

title: Projections of human papillomavirus (HPV) vaccination impact on non-cervical cancer outcomes among women in 117 low- and middle-income countries: a modelling study.
abstract: INTRODUCTION: Human papillomavirus (HPV) is a leading cause of both cervical and non-cervical cancers, including anal, oropharyngeal, vaginal and vulvar cancers. While most HPV vaccination impact assessments have focused on preventing cervical cancer among women, the broader benefits of vaccination against other HPV-attributable cancers in low- and middle-income countries (LMICs) remain less explored. METHODS: We used a static cohort model to assess the potential health impact of bivalent HPV vaccination on HPV-attributable female non-cervical cancers in 117 LMICs from 2030 to 2100. The model incorporated country-specific data on cancer mortality, HPV type distribution, demographic projections and vaccine coverage. Sensitivity analyses were performed to account for uncertainties in cancer incidence, cancer mortality and HPV type distribution. RESULTS: Our projections suggest that HPV vaccination could contribute to prevention of approximately five 90 000 cases of anal, 880 000 cases of oropharyngeal, 1.27 million cases of vaginal and 2.18 million cases of vulvar cancers over the analytic period. In total, 3.02 million deaths from these non-cervical cancers among women could be averted by 2100. The African region is expected to see the largest relative reductions in both cases and deaths while the European region showed the smallest gains. By the end of the century, 58 countries are projected to reach at least a 25% reduction in anal cancer mortality compared with just 25 countries for oropharyngeal cancer. These findings reflect substantial regional disparities in both burden and vaccination impact. CONCLUSION: HPV vaccination holds considerable promise in reducing the burden of non-cervical cancers among women in LMICs, especially in regions with high incidence and limited access to care. Recognising and harnessing these broader benefits can strengthen the public health case for scaling up vaccine access, implementing region-specific strategies and investing in equitable healthcare systems to decrease global disparities.

title: Preliminary Development and Assessment of a Multiplex Assay for Human Papillomavirus Antibody Detection Using Commercial L1 Proteins
abstract: BACKGROUND: Human papillomavirus (HPV)-associated cancers are preventable with vaccination. Serologic assays monitor antibody responses, but their complexity and cost pose limitations when evaluating population level immunity. We developed an L1-based assay for the detection of multiple type-specific HPV antibodies. METHODS: The Luminex-based assay used recombinant L1 proteins from seven HPVs (HPV-6/11/16/18/35/45/58) for the detection of type-specific immunoglobulin (Ig)G and IgA. Cutoffs were established using plasma from infants and children. The assay was optimized and qualified using a sample set from a blinded proficiency panel developed at the Frederick National Laboratory for Cancer Research. RESULTS: Sensitivity and specificity for anti-HPV-6/11/16/18/58 IgG were 100% at the Mean + 3 standard deviation [SD] and Mean + 5 SD thresholds. Sensitivity for HPV-45 was 100% and 92.9% at the +3 SD and +5 SD thresholds, respectively. IgA detection showed moderate positivity among vaccinated individuals, with peak estimates of 96.4% (HPV-11) and 85.7% (HPV-58) at the +3 SD threshold. IgA was correlated with IgG (Spearman's ρ = 0.74). The L1-assay differentiated high, intermediate, low, and negative response groups from the blinded samples for all HPV genotypes (p < 0.0001). CONCLUSION: The L1-binding assay has the potential to be a scalable option for high-throughput detection of broad-spectrum HPV immunoglobulins, but further standardization and validation are needed.

analysis.summary_en: This study aimed to develop and assess a multiplex assay for detecting type-specific HPV antibodies using commercial L1 proteins. The L1-based assay was designed to detect IgG and IgA antibodies against seven HPV types (6, 11, 16, 18, 35, 45, and 58). The assay was optimized and validated using a blinded proficiency panel. The study provides a foundation for improving serologic monitoring of HPV immunity, which could support public health efforts in vaccination programs.

abstract_zh: 背景:通过疫苗接种可以预防与人乳头瘤病毒(HPV)相关的癌症。血清学检测方法用于监测抗体反应,但在评估群体水平免疫力时,其复杂性和成本存在局限性。我们开发了一种基于L1的检测方法,用于检测多种型特异性HPV抗体。方法:该基于Luminex的检测方法使用来自七种HPV(HPV-6/11/16/18/35/45/58)的重组L1蛋白,用于检测型特异性免疫球蛋白(Ig)G和IgA。使用婴儿和儿童的血浆建立了截断值。该检测方法通过由弗雷德里克国家癌症研究中心开发的盲样能力验证面板样本集进行优化和验证。结果:对于抗HPV-6/11/16/18/58 IgG,使用均值+3标准差[SD]和均值+5 SD阈值时,灵敏度和特异性均为100%。对于HPV-45,灵敏度在+3 SD阈值时为100%,在+5 SD阈值时为92.9%。在疫苗接种者中,IgA检测显示出中等阳性反应,其中在+3 SD阈值时,HPV-11的峰值估计为96.4%,HPV-58的峰值估计为85.7%。IgA与IgG呈正相关(Spearman's ρ = 0.74)。该L1检测方法能够根据盲样样本区分所有HPV基因型的高、中等、低和阴性反应组(p < 0.0001)。结论:L1结合检测方法有潜力成为一种可扩展的高通量检测广泛型HPV免疫球蛋白的方法,但需要进一步标准化和验证。科学与公共卫生意义:研究结果表明,基于L1的检测方法可用于监测特定HPV型别的群体免疫力,这对于评估疫苗接种项目的效果具有重要意义。

title: Gelatin–PVA Hydrogel Composite-Based Immunosensing Interface for Early Detection of HPV16-Driven Cervical Cancer
abstract: Abstract Viral oncoprotein HPV16 E6 is a critical mediator of cervical malignancy and a promising biomarker for early-stage detection of cervical cancer. Current diagnostic approaches centered around morphology-based screening and DNA-based assays emphasize the need for noninvasive, affordable, and highly sensitive urine-based detection methods targeting HPV16 E6 oncoprotein for early diagnosis. This study introduces a noninvasive diagnostic strategy using a gelatin–PVA (G-PVA) hydrogel composite-based electrochemical biosensor for HPV16 E6 oncoprotein detection in spiked urine samples. The proposed platform integrates chemically crosslinked G-PVA hydrogel as a transducing matrix for biosensing offering superior biocompatibility, electrochemical stability, and enhanced surface area for antibody immobilization. The biosensor platform demonstrates robust electrochemical performance with a broad dynamic range (1 pg mL–1 to 1 μg mL–1), ultra-low detection limit (0.56 pg mL–1), and quantification limit (1.88 pg mL–1). Furthermore, it exhibits a sensitivity of 37 μA cm–2 log–1 (pg mL–1) along with good reproducibility and specificity toward E6 oncoprotein even in complex media such as artificial urine. Overall, this study demonstrates the feasibility of the G-PVA hydrogel composite-based biosensor as an affordable, noninvasive, point-of-care (POC) detection platform representing significant advancement toward early detection of HPV16-associated cervical cancer.

The results highlight the potential of this biosensor to advance early diagnosis of HPV16-associated cervical cancer.

title_zh: 基于明胶-聚乙烯醇水凝胶复合材料的免疫传感界面用于HPV16驱动的宫颈癌的早期检测
source_body_en: Abstract Viral oncoprotein HPV16 E6 is a critical mediator of cervical malignancy and a promising biomarker for early-stage detection of cervical cancer. Current diagnostic approaches centered around morphology-based screening and DNA-based assays emphasize the need for noninvasive, affordable, and highly sensitive urine-based detection methods targeting HPV16 E6 oncoprotein for early diagnosis. This study introduces a noninvasive diagnostic strategy using a gelatin–PVA (G-PVA) hydrogel composite-based electrochemical biosensor for HPV16 E6 oncoprotein detection in spiked urine samples. The proposed platform integrates chemically crosslinked G-PVA hydrogel as a transducing matrix for biosensing offering superior biocompatibility, electrochemical stability, and enhanced surface area for antibody immobilization. The biosensor platform demonstrates robust electrochemical performance with a broad dynamic range (1 pg mL–1 to 1 μg mL–1), ultra-low detection limit (0.56 pg mL–1), and quantification limit (1.88 pg mL–1). Furthermore, it exhibits a sensitivity of 37 μA cm–2 log–1 (pg mL–1) along with good reproducibility and specificity toward E6 oncoprotein even in complex media such as artificial urine. Overall, this study demonstrates the feasibility of the G-PVA hydrogel composite-based biosensor as an affordable, noninvasive, point-of-care (POC) detection platform representing significant advancement toward early detection of HPV16-associated cervical cancer.
abstract_zh: 摘要 人乳头瘤病毒(HPV)16的癌基因蛋白E6是宫颈恶性肿瘤的关键介导因子,也是早期检测宫颈癌的有前景的生物标志物。目前以形态学筛查和DNA检测为基础的诊断方法强调需要针对HPV16 E6癌基因蛋白的非侵入性、经济实惠且高度敏感的尿液检测方法,以实现早期诊断的检测。本研究引入了一种基于明胶-聚乙烯醇(G-PVA)水凝胶复合材料的电化学生物传感器,用于检测人工尿液样本中HPV16 E6癌基因蛋白。该平台采用化学交联的G-PVA水凝胶作为生物传感的转导基质,具有优异的生物相容性、电化学稳定性以及增强的抗体固定表面积。生物传感器平台表现出稳健的电化学性能,具有广泛的动态范围(1 pg mL–1至1 μg mL–1)、超低检测限(0.56 pg mL–1)和定量限(1.88 pg mL–1)。此外,即使在复杂介质如人工尿液中,该生物传感器也表现出对E6癌基因蛋白的良好灵敏度(37 μA cm–2 log–1 [pg mL–1])以及良好的可重复性和特异性。总体而言,本研究展示了基于G-PVA水凝胶复合材料的生物传感器作为经济实惠、非侵入性、即时检测(POC)平台在HPV16相关宫颈癌早期检测中的可行性,代表了该领域的重要进展。

title: Human Papillomavirus-Related Diseases in Urology: Diagnosis, Treatment, Prevention, and Clinical Considerations for Healthcare Providers
abstract: Human papillomavirus (HPV) has long been regarded as a gynecologic pathogen, yet its disease burden in men is substantial and rapidly increasing. In Korea, the prevalence of anogenital warts in men has tripled over the past decade, penile cancer continues to rise, and HPV-positive oropharyngeal cancer (OPC) incidence in men has already exceeded that of cervical cancer in comparable high-income countries. This review reframes HPV as an urgent urological, occupational, and public health concern. Drawing primarily on the 2023 Korean Sexually Transmitted Infection (STI) Guidelines and the 2021 U.S. Centers for Disease Control and Prevention STI Treatment Guidelines, supplemented by original primary literature retrieved from PubMed, we address: (1) the male-specific epidemiological shift; (2) nonsexual and occupational transmission routes, with particular emphasis on surgical smoke; (3) evidence-based infection control in urology practice; (4) clinical management of anogenital warts; (5) male HPV vaccination policy, international comparisons, and cost-effectiveness; and (6) future research priorities including OPC prevention, HPV and male infertility, and the need for urology-specific infection control guidelines. From 2026, Korea will include 12-year-old boys in its National Immunization Program—the first gender-neutral HPV vaccination policy in Korea. This review highlights the expanding and indispensable role of urologists in HPV management and emphasizes that infection control vigilance and gender-neutral vaccination strategies are essential to reduce the mounting societal burden of HPV-related diseases. This review provides a practical framework for urologists to integrate HPV prevention, infection control, and vaccination counseling into routine clinical practice.

abstract_zh: 人乳头瘤病毒 (HPV) 长期以来被认为是一种妇科病原体,但其在男性中的疾病负担却很大且迅速增加。在韩国,过去十年中男性肛门生殖器疣的 发病率 增加了两倍,阴茎癌持续上升,男性 HPV 阳性口咽癌 (OPC) 发病率 已经超过了可比高收入国家的 发病率。这篇综述将 HPV 重新定义为一个紧迫的泌尿科、职业和公共卫生问题。主要借鉴 2023 年韩国性传播感染 (STI) 指南和 2021 年美国疾病控制与预防中心 STI 治疗 指南,并辅以从 PubMed 检索到的原始原始文献,我们解决了:(1) 男性特异性流行病学转变;(2)非性和职业性的传播途径,特别强调手术烟雾;(3)泌尿外科实践中循证感染控制;(4)肛门生殖器疣的临床治疗;(5)男性HPV 疫苗接种政策、国际比较及成本效益;(6) 未来的研究重点,包括 OPC 预防、HPV 和男性不育,以及泌尿科特定感染控制指南的需求。从 2026 年起,韩国将把 12 岁男孩纳入国家免疫计划,这是韩国首个性别中立的 HPV 疫苗接种 政策。这篇综述强调了泌尿科医师在 HPV 管理中不断扩大且不可或缺的作用,并强调感染控制警惕和性别中立的 疫苗接种 策略对于减少 HPV 相关疾病日益增加的社会负担至关重要。本综述为泌尿科医生提供了一个实用的框架,将 HPV 预防、感染控制和 疫苗接种 咨询纳入常规临床实践。

title: Incidence and Prevalence of Human Papillomavirus Infection to Predict Outcomes from HPV-Based Cervical Cancer Screening in Women and People with a Cervix Living with HIV
abstract: Background: Human papillomavirus (HPV) testing has been implemented in many organized cervix screening programs; however, understanding how this screening methodology affects rates of colposcopy and further follow-up procedures remains underexplored, especially among women with HIV. In the absence of HPV screening program data in British Columbia (BC), Canada, we sought to determine HPV prevalence and estimates for colposcopies among a cohort of women with HIV using the BC Cervix Screening algorithm. Setting: HPV data were collected and analyzed from a prospective HPV vaccine immunogenicity cohort study of women with HIV from 14 sites of HIV care across Canada from 2008 to 2015. Methods: HPV data were obtained during the screening (month −3), baseline (month 0), month 12, and month 24 time points (Linear Array assay). Participant demographic and clinical characteristics (CD4 + count, HIV viral load, etc.) were assessed to determine associations between HPV prevalence and estimates for colposcopy using rate ratios and 95% confidence intervals. Results: Overall, 47.2% of participants had oncogenic HPV detected at screening which would result in a colposcopy referral. In total, 15.9% of participants had oncogenic HPV detected at screening, month 12, and month 24 time points, which would result in 3 consecutive referrals to colposcopy. Participants with repeat oncogenic HPV detected were less likely to have a suppressed HIV viral load compared with participants without oncogenic HPV detected. Conclusions: Results of this study suggest that HPV testing will result in a high proportion of referrals to colposcopy and follow-up procedures among women with HIV, which will require preparation and planning. Further work is needed to provide the appropriate support and education for women with HIV when incorporating HPV testing into cervix screening programs.

analysis.summary_en: This study aimed to assess the impact of HPV testing on colposcopy referral rates among women with HIV in Canada. HPV data were collected from a prospective cohort study across 14 HIV care sites between 2008 and 2015. The Linear Array assay was used to detect oncogenic HPV at screening, baseline, and follow-up time points. Results showed that 47.2% of participants had oncogenic HPV detected at screening, leading to colposcopy referrals, and 15.9% had persistent HPV infections over 24 months, resulting in three consecutive referrals. The authors suggest that these findings highlight the need for preparedness in cervical cancer screening programs for women with HIV, as HPV testing may significantly increase the demand for colposcopy and follow-up procedures. The study provides important insights into the implications of HPV screening in this population but does not report specific limitations or an evidence strength assessment.

elements_zh.study_design_and_population: HPV数据来自一项针对感染HIV女性的前瞻性HPV免疫原性队列研究,该研究在加拿大14个HIV护理中心进行,时间跨度为2008年至2015年。

elements_zh.main_results: 整体而言,47.2%的参与者在筛查阶段检测出致癌型HPV,需转诊至阴道镜检查。共有15.9%的参与者在筛查、第12个月及第24个月时间点均检测出致癌型HPV,需接受3次连续的阴道镜检查转诊。
elements_zh.interpretation_and_novelty: 本研究结果表明,HPV检测将导致感染HIV女性群体中大量阴道镜检查及后续随访程序的转诊,需提前做好准备与规划。
elements_zh.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: 这些发现可以为HIV感染女性的高危型HPV筛查项目制定有针对性的策略提供依据,强调需要充足的资源和随访协议。
elements_zh.limitations_and_evidence_strength: 所提供的证据未报告研究设计的局限性或证据强度评估。

title: Micro-Costing Analysis for Human Papillomavirus (HPV) Vaccination Services for Out-of-School (OOS) Girls in Indonesia: Evidence from a Pilot Study
abstract: Abstract Background: Cervical cancer remains a major public health challenge in Indonesia, with Human Papillomavirus (HPV) infection responsible for nearly all cases. The government has integrated HPV vaccination into the national School Children Immunization Month (BIAS). However, out-of-school (OOS) girls remain difficult to reach because they are not covered by the school-based vaccination platform. This study aimed to estimate the cost of delivering a single-dose HPV vaccination program to OOS girls and to project the national-level cost of scaling up the program. Method: Micro-costing approach was used to estimate both economic and financial costs of delivering HPV vaccination to OOS girls in Bekasi City, Bandar Lampung City, and Bangka Regency. Costs were categorized into outreach and delivery efforts. A scale-up costing analysis was also conducted to estimate national-level costs. Result: The results show that the cost per vaccinated OOS girl aged 11 ranged from US$ 22.77 to 38.55, while the financial cost range from US$ 12.70 to 29.50, varied by implementation context, with outreach activities, transportation, and vaccine delivery supplies identified as the main cost drivers. The estimated national annual economic and financial cost of scaling-up HPV vaccination for OOS girls are US$ 644,215.23 and US$ 483,138.35, respectively. Conclusion: Optimizing OOS girls' outreach and HPV vaccination is essential to achieve sustained full coverage. National cost estimates show that reaching and vaccinating OOS girls accounts for less than 3% of the national immunization budget.

title_zh: 印度尼西亚非在校女生单剂人乳头瘤病毒(HPV)疫苗接种服务的微成本分析:来自试点研究的证据
source_body_en: Abstract Background: Cervical cancer remains a major public health challenge in Indonesia, with Human Papillomavirus (HPV) infection responsible for nearly all cases. The government has integrated HPV vaccination into the national School Children Immunization Month (BIAS). However, out-of-school (OOS) girls remain difficult to reach because they are not covered by the school-based vaccination platform. This study aimed to estimate the cost of delivering a single-dose HPV vaccination program to OOS girls and to project the national-level cost of scaling up the program. Method: Micro-costing approach was used to estimate both economic and financial costs of delivering HPV vaccination to OOS girls in Bekasi City, Bandar Lampung City, and Bangka Regency. Costs were categorized into outreach and delivery efforts. A scale-up costing analysis was also conducted to estimate national-level costs. Result: The results show that the cost per vaccinated OOS girl aged 11 ranged from US$ 22.77 to 38.55, while the financial cost range from US$ 12.70 to 29.50, varied by implementation context, with outreach activities, transportation, and vaccine delivery supplies identified as the main cost drivers. The estimated national annual economic and financial cost of scaling-up HPV vaccination for OOS girls are US$ 644,215.23 and US$ 483,138.35, respectively. Conclusion: Optimizing OOS girls' outreach and HPV vaccination is essential to achieve sustained full coverage. National cost estimates show that reaching and vaccinating OOS girls accounts for less than 3% of the national immunization budget.
abstract_zh: 摘要 背景:人乳头瘤病毒(HPV)感染是印度尼西亚宫颈癌的主要病因,而政府已将HPV疫苗接种纳入全国学校儿童免疫月(BIAS)。然而,非在校女生(OOS)由于未被学校平台覆盖,仍难以触及。本研究旨在估算向非在校女生提供单剂HPV疫苗接种计划的成本,并预测该计划在国家层面扩大规模后的成本。方法:采用微成本分析方法,估算在雅加达市、巴淡市和邦加县向非在校女生提供HPV疫苗接种计划的经济成本和财务成本。成本被分为外展和接种活动。还进行了扩大规模的成本分析,以估算国家层面的成本。结果:结果显示,11岁接种HPV疫苗的非在校女生每人成本范围为22.77至38.55美元,而财务成本范围为12.70至29.50美元,成本因实施背景而异,外展活动、交通和疫苗接种物资被确定为主要成本驱动因素。扩大HPV疫苗接种计划覆盖非在校女生的国家年度经济和财务成本估计分别为644,215.23美元和483,138.35美元。结论:优化非在校女生的外展和HPV疫苗接种对于实现持续全面覆盖至关重要。国家成本估算表明,接触和接种非在校女生仅占国家免疫预算的不到3%。

title: A systematic review and meta-analysis of human papillomavirus genotype distribution in condyloma acuminata: divergent profiles in HIV-positive and HIV-negative patients
abstract: Condyloma acuminata, chiefly linked to low-risk human papillomavirus (LR-HPV), demonstrates a more severe clinical course – characterized by extensive lesions, recurrence, and treatment resistance–in HIV individuals. This group also shows increased high-risk HPV (HR-HPV) infection and coinfection prevalence, elevating oncogenic risk. This review aimed to compare HPV subtype profiles between HIV-positive and HIV-negative patients to guide clinical strategies. A systematic review and meta-analysis was conducted, querying PubMed, ScienceDirect, Cochrane/CENTRAL, and Google Scholar for literature published from 2015 to 2025. Six studies involving 703 participants were included. Data were synthesized using a random-effects model in RevMan 5.4.1 to generate pooled odds ratios with 95% confidence intervals. Methodological quality was evaluated via ROBINS-I and SIGN tools. Results demonstrated that HIV status was a significant determinant of HPV genotype distribution. Individuals living with HIV had substantially higher frequencies of HR-HPV infections (e.g. genotypes 16, 18, 52, 59) compared with HIV-negative individuals, in whom LR-HPV types predominated (pooled odds ratio: 5.25; 95% confidence interval: 3.10–8.88; P <0.001). In summary, these findings confirm a distinct HR-HPV predominance in individuals living with HIV, underscoring the imperative for enhanced, tailored screening, and preventive oncology measures in this high-risk group.

title: Intratumoral Human Papillomavirus in Advanced Prostate Cancer: Systematic Review, Meta-Analysis, and Real-World Evidence from the Largest Cohort to Date
abstract: The etiopathogenesis of prostate cancer (PCa) is complex and involves multiple hormonal and environmental factors. Among these, the role of infectious agents remains controversial. Human papillomavirus (HPV) is known to promote carcinogenesis in epithelial tumors and has also been detected, albeit inconsistently, in PCa tissues. This systematic review, meta-analysis, and real-world cohort study aimed to clarify the prevalence and the prognostic role of intratumoral (IT)-HPV detection in locally advanced and metastatic PCa. We performed a systematic literature search including studies reporting IT-HPV detection in locally advanced (LA-PCa) and metastatic PCa (mPCa). Pooled prevalence estimates were calculated using random-effects models. In parallel, HPV DNA was analyzed using archival tissue in a single-center real-world retrospective cohort of 196 metastatic PCa patients. Twenty-three records met the inclusion criteria, comprising 22 full-text publications and one abstract. Nineteen datasets, encompassing 837 patients, contributed to the quantitative synthesis of stage III–IV disease. Pooled IT-HPV prevalence in mPCa was 18.5% (95% CI, 6.4–34%), while including also LA-PCa was 14.6% (95% CI, 5.2–26.8). Eastern countries showed higher IT-HPV prevalence in both mPCa and LA-PCa (40% and 34.3%, respectively) compared with Western regions (0.8% and 0.3%; p 7) in advanced stage (pooled OR 6.32, 95% CI, 3.13–12.78) compared with IT-HPV-negative PCa; however, no studies reported data on its association with survival outcomes. Within our retrospective cohort, IT-HPV DNA was detected in 3.1% of cases (6/196) and exhibited typical PCa driver alterations, such as TP53, SPOP, PIK3CA, and AR amplification. IT–HPV seems to be infrequent in metastatic and locally advanced PCa in Western populations and more prevalent in Asian cohorts and might be associated with a higher Gleason score. IT–HPV-positive advanced PCa seems to exhibit typical PCa driver alterations. Data on the association between IT–HPV status and survival outcomes in PCa are lacking. Standardized molecular assays and multicenter prospective studies are needed to delineate its significance in PCa.
